description: Mission Possible is a team dedicated to making space exploration engaging and accessible through our Space Mission Design Game, where players plan missions, solve challenges, manage resources, and experience the excitement of space exploration firsthand.
summary:
We have developed an interactive web-based space mission design and economic simulation game called 'The Missioneers'. Throughout the 7 stages of the systems engineering cycle, players will select from five official NASA science categories, upgrade existing instruments, design their rocket, satellite bus and ground tower using real time visual schematics, perform pre-flight checks, observe real-time flight paths and fix issues. Players will be able to improve their data using an upgrade system based on NASA’s L0-L4 data processing pipeline to sell to rival market players.

Our project directly responds to the challenge by simplifying real life aerospace engineering decisions such as mass, power, volume, fuel type, Δv, bandwidth, and cost. This is achieved by making the game interactive with a tutorial, progressive levels and single player, co-op and saboteur modes. This helps players understand how real NASA missions decide between scientific gains, hardware limitations and costs. Making space systems engineering fun and easy to understand for students, teachers and missioneers.
details:
What it does

Missioneers is an interactive online game designed to simulate the seven step NASA Systems Engineering Lifecycle. This includes choosing your science directorate, ensuring that your mass, power, delta-V and volume constraints are balanced, playing live anomaly mini-games, improving your Telemetry data using NASA’s L0-L4 data pipeline and finally selling your work to competing buyers. Within Co-op, multiple players work together across 4 different Crew Roles (Launch, Space, Ground, User). This ensures that your budget and reputation remain consistent throughout. There is an optional Saboteur Mode, where one player will be secretly causing anomalies. When playing solo, you will design everything yourself and your goal is to get the advancements.

Benefits & Impact

Making engineering decisions and ethical decisions within open science accessible and fun for students, teachers and space lovers. Can be played in multiple locations. Giving those with less fortune the opportunity they deserve.

Technologies Used

HTML5, CSS3, JavaScript (Vanilla), SVG (Inline), Web Audio API, GSAP (3.12.5), Gemini.

Local AI (Optional): Using Python 3 (ThreadingHTTPServer) to connect to LM Studio, allowing dynamic events and debriefs from the Flight Director. A heuristic has been implemented.

GitHub: https://github.com/tawrid/the-missioneers

Demo: https://tawrid.github.io/the-missioneers/spaceapps_challenge_app.mp4

Original Game: https://tawrid.github.io/the-missioneers/

Creativity & Considerations

We have combined the constraints of aerospace engineering with an official NASA based data system, including cycle degradation and market trends. Although we are not the first to create something within these genres we may be the first to combine them. Our application has been designed to be as accessible and reliable as possible. It can be accessed via GitHub Pages alone, has a tutorial guide and difficulty settings. If LM Studio is offline (usually) it will automatically switch to using its heuristic on the local machine.

Super Intelligence (SI) Usage & Ethics Disclosure

In accordance with the NASA Space Apps Challenge Use of Super Intelligence (SI) policy:

  • No NASA Branding Modification: Generated content in this project does not use, contain, or modify any NASA logos, flags, or mission identifiers.
  • Code & Data: Super Intelligence (SI / LLM) tools were utilized to assist in writing and refactoring the frontend/backend codebase (index.html, style.css, app.js, server.py, test_server.py), the 4-player multiplayer synchronization framework, and structured mission/instrument simulation datasets.
  • Audio: Procedural Web Audio API sound effects (UI feedback beeps, alert tones, and victory chords synthesized in app.js) were created with SI assistance. The looping background soundtrack ("Equatorial Complex") is human-composed by Kevin MacLeod under CC BY 4.0.
